parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem:
Table 9.1 shows the mass defects of three nuclei.

Table 9.1

| nucleus | mass defect / u |
| $^{2}_{1}\text{H}$ | 0.002388 |
| $^{3}_{1}\text{H}$ | 0.009105 |
| $^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ | 0.030377 |

The nuclear fusion process in a particular star is described by

$$^{2}_{1}\text{H} + ^{3}_{1}\text{H} \rightarrow ^{4}_{2}\text{He} + \text{X}$$

where X is a particle that has no mass defect.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: State the name of particle X.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Show that the energy released when one nucleus of $^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ is formed in this fusion reaction is $2.8 \times 10^{-12} \text{J}$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.part_stem:
The star in (b) has a radius of $2.3 \times 10^{9} \text{m}$ and a luminosity of $1.4 \times 10^{28} \text{W}$. All the energy released from the formation of $^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ is radiated away from the star. All the energy that is radiated from the star has been released in the formation of $^{4}_{2}\text{He}$.

Determine:

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: the mass of $^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ produced per unit time by the fusion process

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: the surface temperature of the star.
